question: What do we call a positively charged ion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**a cation**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A positively charged ion is called a cation.**
 
• An ion is **an atom or molecule with a net electrical charge.**
 
• A cation **has more protons than electrons,** giving it a positive charge
 
• A hydrogen atom that has lost its electron is a cation with a positive charge,** represented as H+.**
 
• **A calcium ion has a net charge of +2,** which represents the relationship between the number of protons in calcium and the number of electrons in its most stable form

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anions**

 
 
• Anions are** negatively charged ions **that are formed when an atom or molecule gains one or more electrons.
 
• **Examples: **Chloride ion (Cl⁻), Sulfate ion (SO₄²⁻), Nitrate ion (NO₃⁻)
 
• It is **Commonly found in ionic compounds like salts.**
 
 
 
• **Molecule**
 
 
• **​**A **molecule is a group of two or more atoms **bonded together chemically, representing the smallest unit of a chemical compound that can exist independently while retaining the compound's chemical properties.
 
• It can be **either polar (unequal sharing of electrons, e.g., H₂O) or non-polar (equal sharing of electrons, e.g., N₂).**
 
• **Examples: **Water (H₂O), Oxygen (O₂), Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
